Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 79, verse 34–46:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So when the Great Calamity (al-Tammah al-Kubra) comes﴾. Al-Tammah is the event that overwhelms everything else, i.e., it rises above it. Regarding what is meant by it here, there are three opinions.

The first: it is the second blast (al-nafkhah al-thaniyah) in which resurrection takes place.

The second: it is when it is said to the people of the Fire: "Go forth into the Fire."

The third: it is when the people of the Garden are driven to the Garden and the people of the Fire to the Fire.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On that day man will remember what he strove for﴾, i.e., what he did of good and evil. ﴿And Hellfire will be brought forth for whoever sees﴾, i.e., for the sight of the onlookers. Muqatil said: the covering will be removed from it and the creation will look upon it. Abu Mijlaz and Ibn al-Sumayfa' recited "li-man tara" with a ta'. Ibn 'Abbas and Mu'adh al-Qari' recited "li-man ra'a" with a hamzah between the ra' and the alif.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿As for he who transgressed﴾ in his disbelief ﴿and preferred the worldly life﴾ over the Hereafter, ﴿indeed, Hellfire will be his refuge﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: i.e., it will be his refuge. This is the answer to ﴿So when the Great Calamity comes﴾, for the matter is as such.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But as for he who feared the standing before his Lord﴾ — we have mentioned it in Surat al-Rahman [55:46].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And restrained the soul from desire﴾, i.e., from what it desires of the forbidden things. Muqatil said: it is the man who intends to commit sin, then remembers his standing for reckoning, and so abandons it.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They ask you about the Hour, when it will occur﴾ — it has preceded in [al-A'raf: 187]. ﴿In what [position] are you to mention it?﴾, i.e., you are not in any part of its knowledge or mention. The meaning is that you do not know it. ﴿To your Lord is its finality﴾, i.e., the end of its knowledge. ﴿You are only a warner to those who fear it﴾. Abu Ja'far recited "mundhiru" with tanwin. The meaning of the speech is: you are only a fearful warner to those who fear it. The meaning is: your warning benefits only those who fear it, namely the believer in it. As for one who does not fear it, it is as if he was not warned. ﴿It will be as if they﴾ — meaning the disbelievers of Quraysh — ﴿on the day they see it﴾, i.e., witness the Resurrection, ﴿had not remained﴾ in the world. It was said: in their graves, ﴿except for an evening or its morning﴾, i.e., the length of the late part of the day after the afternoon, or its beginning until the sun rises. Al-Zajjaj said: the ha' and alif in "duha-ha" refer back to "ashiyyah" (evening). The meaning: except an evening, or the forenoon of the evening. Al-Farra' said:

If it is said: does the evening have a forenoon? Duha belongs only to the early part of the day?

The answer: this is common in Arabic speech, that they say: "I will come to you in the evening, or its morning; or I will come to you in the morning, or its evening." So "evening" carries the sense of "late," and "morning" carries the sense of "early." One of the Banu 'Uqayl recited to me:

We attacked 'Amir in his house at the evening of the crescent or its last part.

He meant: the evening of the crescent, or the evening of the last part of the evening. This is stronger than their saying: "I will come to you in the morning or its evening."
